description:
FILED s446j (agent J) as #505's residue, MEASURED not guessed.  perl resolves ${EXPR} through the value's STRING form for a number too, so `no strict 'refs'; my $n = 5; ${$n}` reads $5 (undef, read-only) and PCL answers 5 -- p-cast-$'s `(t inner)` fallback returning the number unchanged.  The obvious fix (stringify and take the symbolic path) was IMPLEMENTED and then WITHDRAWN in the same session, and the reason is the finding: PCL's box model loses the reference wrapper on the way out of a container.  %p-hash-unbox-elem returns the REFERENT box for a scalar ref, so `\42` stored in a hash element and read back arrives at p-cast-$ as box(42) with is-ref NIL -- indistinguishable from the box of `my $n = 42` (probed live through the runtime, not inferred).  The cost of guessing wrong is real: Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t row 24 (Moo's `local $self->{captures} = {}` then a nested write) printed nothing where perl prints 42.  A name-exists heuristic ("treat the number as a name only when $N is bound") is WORSE, not better: $1..$20 are always bound, so a hard ref to the number 5 would read $5 -- do NOT retry it.  What would unblock this: a referent-kind distinction that survives the container read (the #154 family; s335 ruled NO new box slot, so it has to come from keeping the wrapper -- i.e. %p-hash-unbox-elem stops stripping a scalar-ref box -- which is a representation change with a full-sweep blast radius and needs a design call).  Until then the STRING spelling is correct (s446j) and the numeric one is guarded by the CANARY row in Pl/t/prefix-incr-deref-01.t, which FAILS when this closes.

RULED s449 (Fable, 2026-08-29): PARKED behind the boxed-aggregates design (post-v0.1; standing ruling: Fable design first, do not start).  The unblocking change -- a container read KEEPING the scalar-ref wrapper (%p-hash-unbox-elem stops stripping) -- is a representation change in exactly that family with a full-sweep blast radius; standalone now pays the blast twice.  Until then: the STRING spelling stays correct (s446j); the numeric spelling stays guarded by the CANARY row in Pl/t/prefix-incr-deref-01.t (fails when this closes); s335 "no new box slot" stands; do NOT retry the name-exists heuristic (this task-s own warning).  The citable record is ir-spec SS8-s existing paragraph naming this task as owner -- no separate not-supported entry.
subject: A NUMERIC symbolic-ref name (`${$n}` with $n == 5 is $5) cannot be told from a hard ref in the box model: %p-hash-unbox-elem hands back the REFERENT box, so `\42` out of a container is byte for byte `my $n = 42`
